Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: ne-groomer[bot]
Message:
test(nousergon-auth): add vitest suite, wire into CI gate (#22)

Zero test files existed despite vitest being wired ("test": "vitest run"
already declared) — this was the tracked remainder of the CI-gate work
(alpha-engine-config-I2527/PR13), which shipped typecheck+build without
tests. Adds real coverage for the service's core surfaces and blocks both
PRs and pre-deploy on it passing.

- src/server.ts, src/auth.ts: minimal refactor to expose test seams
  (createRequestListener(authInstance), createAuth(options)) without
  changing runtime behavior — `node dist/server.js` still binds a real
  port via an import.meta.url entrypoint guard; the module-level `auth`
  singleton is unchanged for production callers.
- 31 tests across 5 files: /health + CORS (server.test.ts), betterAuth
  config wiring + JWKS (auth.test.ts), the allowlist-gate route handler's
  full contract — uniform responses, product-scoping, returning-user
  bypass, validation ordering (allowlist-gate.test.ts), email.ts's
  fail-loud contract, and the magic-link HTML template.
- Hermetic: every test builds an isolated betterAuth instance against a
  fresh SQLite file under os.tmpdir() (never under the repo), migrated
  in-process via better-auth's own getMigrations()/runMigrations() —
  no real credentials anywhere (RESEND_API_KEY is left unset throughout;
  BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is a fixed non-secret test string). Distinct
  x-forwarded-for per request avoids cross-test collisions with the
  magic-link plugin's own per-IP rate limit.
- ci.yml / deploy.yml: `npm test` added as a step in the existing
  "typecheck + build" job in both files — job/check-context name
  unchanged (required status check on main), no branch-protection change
  needed.
- tsconfig.build.json + vitest.config.ts: keep *.test.ts out of the
  shipped dist/ build while still typechecking them via `npm run
  typecheck`.

Verified the suite actually catches regressions: temporarily neutered the
allowlist-gate's rejection branch locally, confirmed 2 tests went red,
reverted.

Validated locally (Node 20, matching CI): npm install && npm run
typecheck && npm run build && npm test all pass clean; also smoke-tested
the real dist/server.js entrypoint (GET /health -> 200 ok).

Closes nousergon/alpha-engine-config#2546
